Subject: Performance/SLO VPC network qualification — ACME Corp

Hi Jordan / Alex —

Thanks for the call earlier today. Quick recap and next steps from Redwood's side to validate the performance/SLOs for a Private (VPC) deployment: 

Summary of ACME requirements we captured:
- Latency: 95th percentile tail for text-generation responses <= 200ms (goal 150ms) end-to-end from ACME app to Redwood model outputs.
- Concurrency/Throughput: target sustained 500 concurrent requests (streaming-enabled), peak bursts to ~1,200.
- Streaming: token-streaming required; clients will open long-lived streaming connections for low-latency partial tokens.
- Request profile: avg prompt 256 tokens, generation up to 512 tokens, expected token throughput ~60k tokens/minute.
- Security/network: deployment inside ACME VPC with either AWS Direct Connect / GCP Interconnect or site-to-site VPN; requirement for minimal egress checks and no transit via public internet where possible.

Immediate asks from our side to run a performance qualification: 
1) Network path diagram (VPC/subnets, NAT/gateway, any transit gateways, firewall appliances) — attach if possible.
2) Preferred connectivity: Direct Connect/Interconnect or site-to-site VPN? If VPN, please share expected one-way additional latency/SLA.
3) IP ranges and egress NAT behavior so we can validate TLS termination and certificate pins.
4) Any proxy/load-balancer in path that may buffer streaming traffic (ALB, NLB, proxies).
5) Expected internal north-south and east-west one-way latencies inside ACME cloud (app -> public subnet -> TPU/GPU placement).

Redwood recommendation (preliminary): for your SLOs we typically target an internal network budget of <= 10ms one-way between the application-facing edge (NAT/LB) and the inference hosts; anything above ~25ms internal significantly increases tail latency risk for streaming workloads. We'll also run a controlled load test that exercises long-lived streaming and token-by-token emission to measure tail behavior.

Attachments: we attached our redwood-vpc-network-checklist.pdf and a sample network_diagram_v1.pdf (stub) to help with the info request.

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- Jordan: please send network diagram + expected VPN/DirectConnect latency by EOD Tue (2026-03-16).
- Redwood (Vivek/Rafael): once we have diagrams, schedule an on-site/virtual network deep-dive and a 2-hour perf-run window to capture tail latencies.

Thanks — let me know if I've missed anything.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear recap. Attaching an initial network diagram and a short VPN config snippet. Some quick answers up front: 

- Connectivity: ACME will prefer Direct Connect (AWS) for production; we can stand up a site-to-site VPN for initial testing.
- VPN latency: our VPN gateway has historically added ~18-25ms one-way when routed through our Palo Alto appliances. Direct Connect expected <5ms one-way to the target AZs you recommended.
- We do have an internal proxy in front of the service mesh for HTTP traffic (Envoy), but streaming TCP passthrough is possible if we route via NLB + proxy bypass. We need your team to confirm TLS handling/termination expectations.
- Concurrency: we can provision a test pool to hit 600 concurrent streaming sessions for the perf window; sustained load to 500 is fine.

Attachments in this message: acme_network_diag_v1.pdf, vpn_config_snippet.txt.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) During streaming tests do you need public IP egress from our side or can we peer privately with static routes?
2) Can you confirm the internal latency budget you suggested (<=10ms one-way) and whether that assumes model local KV cache is colocated with the inference hosts?

Happy to hop on a short call Friday if helpful.

—Jordan

Jordan / Alex —

Appreciate the diagram and config. Quick answers and clarifications: 

- Private peering is preferred for the production rollout (Direct Connect). For initial perf validation, VPN is OK but expect an extra ~20ms tail as you noted — we'll include that in our SLO risk matrix.
- Redwood can operate with private peering + static routes; public egress is not required. We will provide a small set of static IPs to allow through ACME firewalls for the test window.
- Internal latency budget: yes, our <=10ms one-way recommendation assumes inference hosts (GPU pool + KV cache) are in the same AZ/rack and reachable with minimal switching hops. If your app front-ends are in a different AZ or transit via an appliance, add expected hops to the budget.

Action items / next steps: 
1) Jordan: confirm preferred test window (we proposed Wed 2026-03-18 09:00-11:00 PT) and provide any NAT/firewall ACLs needed for our test IPs.
2) ACME: please share traceroute/mtr from the app front-end to the proposed Redwood test IPs (we'll hand over the IPs before the test).
3) Redwood (Vivek/Rafael): prepare perf plan that includes streaming token-by-token emission, 95/99 tail captures, and a run with both VPN and Direct Connect emulation.

I'll schedule the perf-run calendar invite once we lock the window. If Direct Connect is delayed, we'll still run the VPN-based test and annotate expected production deltas.

Best,
Marissa

Looping in a few quick engineering notes ahead of the perf run: 

- Peering vs VPN: strongly recommend Direct Connect for production; for the perf window we will run tests both over VPN (to capture realistic degradation) and over our isolated interconnect (if ACME can provision Direct Connect test circuits).
- Model/Runtime config: for streaming at 500 concurrent requests with 512-token generations we recommend: quantized FP16 runtime, dynamic batching with max batch size 32, and per-worker concurrency limited to 16 streams to avoid head-of-line blocking. We'll also enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts which reduces end-to-end token emission.
- Network tuning: set TCP keepalive and lower idle timeouts for proxies (Envoy) to avoid reset during long-lived streams. Use NLB in TCP passthrough mode to preserve client congestion behavior for low-latency emissions.
- Observability: please enable packet capture on ingress to the LB during the run and share pcap for 10 minutes around peak to help diagnose spikes.

I'll draft the perf plan doc and share by EOD today; Rafael/Neha can help with test harness and load generation.

Thanks,
Vivek
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
